summary: Nicolaas Johannes Krom studied at Leiden University (Ph.D. 1908) under J. H. C. Kern and J. S. Speyer. A scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, he worked at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies and held professorships at Leiden University (1919, 1925–1945).

Nicolaas van Wijk was a linguist who studied at the Universities of Amsterdam, Leipzig, and Moscow under C. C. Uhlenbeck, Karl Brugmann, August Leskien, and F. F. Fortunatov. He worked at the National Library of the Netherlands (1907) and became Professor at Leiden University in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey works in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004) and held a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012–2013) and was supervised by Claudine Bautze-Picron, Peter Skilling, and Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h. He held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016–2017).
Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He served as Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010).

Nicolas Tournadre is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle under Claude Hagège. He held posts at INALCO, Paris 8 University, the University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University (professor, ~2011–2020).
Nicole Baden works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Richard Baker, whom she succeeded in 2024.

Nicole Balbir was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She held posts at Patna University (1952–1955) and at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1974–1992).

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. She held posts at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (later INALCO, ~1946–1977) and taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre (~1963–1976).

Nicolás Altuchow was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak (~1934–1939). He taught linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of the Republic (1951–1982) and held a post at the National Museum of Natural History.
Nidheesh Kannan B. is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (2016–2018). In 2021, he held a post there as an Assistant Professor.

Niels Ludvig Westergaard was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, and Oxford. At the University of Copenhagen, he served as Lektor (1844), Professor (1850), and Rector (1867–1868).

Niels Studsgaard Fuglsang, a scholar in Indology, studied at the University of Copenhagen (1778). He served as a minister at Zion Church in Tranquebar (1792–1804) and became a member of The Asiatic Society in 1801.
Nigel Allan worked in history and archaeology, succeeding Marianne Winder. He served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Trust (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray studied at Calcutta, UCL, and Leiden (under Jean Philippe Vogel). An Indologist and historian, he served as Chief Librarian (1936) and Professor of Fine Arts (1946–1965) at Calcutta University, and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965–1970).

Nijun Zhang is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. She studied at Beijing Foreign Studies University (BA 2018–2022) and the University of Pittsburgh (MA 2023–2025), before undertaking doctoral studies at the University of Virginia (2025).

Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna under Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008) and completed her Mag. phil. under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010).
Nikita Yakovlevich Bichurin was a scholar of Sinology and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique (~1826–1853).

Niklas Luhmann was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1946–1949), Harvard University (~1960–1961), and Bielefeld University. He held an academic post at Bielefeld University from ~1968 to 1993.
Niklas Müller was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz until 1788. He served as Conservator at the Städtische Kunstsammlungen Mainz in 1805.
